processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental steel was melted and cast in a 50 kg vacuum induction furnace and then air cooled to RT.
The ingot was reheated to 1250 °C and held for 2 h for homogenization.
Ingot forged into round bars with a diameter of 60 mm followed by cooling to RT in the furnace; starting and finishing forging temperatures were 1100 and 950 °C.
Instrumented Charpy impact test on 10 × 10 × 55 mm specimens with a 2 mm depth V-notch using a PST752H-4 WANCE impact tester.

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic equiaxed grain structure (single phase); no isothermal martensite forms at -196 °C, indicating a very stable austenite.

Cross-section near the impact fracture surface after testing at -196 °C: primary crack path is zigzag; most regions show transgranular fracture; only a few regions experienced planar glide during impact deformation.

defects.lattice_distortion: significant local orientation gradient adjacent to the primary cracks within grain interiors

defects.type: planar glide / slip-band traces (few localized regions)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Primary crack propagation path at the fracture surface exhibits a zigzag shape and most regions show transgranular fracture; the misorientation difference between the regions on both sides of the crack is less than 15°, implying the two regions were in the same grain before cracking.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar glide is observed only in a few regions near the fracture after impact at -196 °C (sparse, locally confined slip-band traces); planar glide is difficult to activate at low temperature under high strain rate.
interfaces.interface_notes: Secondary cracks were present only in the sample tested at RT, not at -196 °C; the -196 °C sample shows no secondary cracks.

measurement_conditions.environment: Charpy impact test; specimen tested in liquid nitrogen
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: 10 × 10 × 55 mm with a 2 mm depth V-notch
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Instrumented Charpy impact test on a PST752H-4 WANCE impact tester; load-deflection curves recorded.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Tested at -196 °C; specimens 10 × 10 × 55 mm with a 2 mm depth V-notch; load-deflection curves recorded
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the impact load-deflection response and absorbed energy at cryogenic temperature
characterization_methods.key_findings: W_all = 188 J; W_initiation = 112 J; peak load just above 30 kN; RC = 10.9957; F_in almost equal to F_m.

characterization_methods.technique: Fracture surface observation by SEM and 3D optical microscopy
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: VHX-5000 ultra-depth of field 3D microscope and SEM
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Fracture surface and radial zone after Charpy impact at -196 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the macroscopic and microscopic fracture morphology
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fracture surface appeared significantly flatter; combination of ductile and brittle fracture; high-density large dimples and tear edges indicating quasi-cleavage cracks.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apreo S HiVac SEM; Gatan/685.C automated argon ion-beam cross-section polishing
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cross-section near the fracture surface; EBSD step size 0.8 μm
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze the microstructure near the fracture surface and the crack path
characterization_methods.key_findings: Primary crack path is zigzag; most regions show transgranular fracture; misorientation difference across the crack is less than 15°.

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of regions near fracture
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Regions near the fracture after Charpy impact at -196 °C (20 µm scale bar)
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe planar-glide/slip-band features near the fracture
characterization_methods.key_findings: Only few regions experienced planar glide; the planar-glide/slip-band traces are sparse and confined to small localised regions.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The computed SFE at -196 °C (32 mJ/m²) is consistent with the observed suppression of DIMT and occurrence of mechanical twinning/planar glide.

SFE of the experimental steel estimated at 32, 40 and 61 mJ/m² for -196 °C, -77 °C and RT respectively; the -196 °C value (32 mJ/m²) is within the 18–35 mJ/m² window where mechanical twinning is the main mechanism.

unmapped_findings: Charpy impact absorbed energy W_all of the Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si steel at -196 °C is 188 J (compared with 277 J at -77 °C and 327 J at RT).
Crack initiation energy W_initiation at -196 °C is 112 J (compared with 68 J at -77 °C and 57 J at RT); the high W_initiation indicates stronger resistance to crack initiation at lower temperature.

Rebound compliance (RC, absolute slope from F_iu to F_a) at -196 °C is 10.9957 (compared with 4.6215 at -77 °C and 3.7864 at RT), indicating that unstable cracks propagate more rapidly at lower temperature.
At -196 °C the crack initiation load F_in is almost equal to the maximum load F_m because no obvious change occurs in the slope of the compliance-changing-rate (CCR) curve.
The ratio F_iu/F_m at -196 °C approaches ~0.98 (compared with ~0.83 at RT), suggesting cracks rapidly propagate from the stable to the unstable regime.
Characteristic impact loads at -196 °C (Fig. 9): general yield load F_gy ≈ 22 kN, maximum load F_m ≈ 32 kN, crack initiation load F_in ≈ 31.5 kN.
The load-deflection curve of the -196 °C impact sample peaks just above 30 kN at ~4 mm deflection and terminates near 10 mm deflection.
Only few regions experienced planar glide during impact deformation at -196 °C (sparse, locally confined slip bands), which explains the weak resistance to crack propagation at this temperature.
The fracture surface of the impact sample tested at -196 °C appeared significantly flatter than at -77 °C and RT, and no obvious fibrous zone was observed at -196 °C.
Secondary cracks were observed near the fracture after impact testing at RT but not at -196 °C; their absence at -196 °C is associated with the lower crack propagation energy.
